learning_outcomes.text: Develop the theoretical and practical skills necessary for implementing strategies for the management and security of a computer network.
Understanding of the main security issues affecting systems and networks.
Knowledge and understanding of the security protocols and strategies provided by the TCP/IP stack.
Knowledge and understanding of Software-Defined Networks.
Knowledge and understanding of tools for ensuring system and network security.
Knowledge and understanding of protocols and tools for network management.
Configure hosts and network devices appropriately.
Apply system configurations to improve security.
Use virtualization environments to validate network configurations.
Use POSIX BASH for network host management.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course and to cyber security
Introduction to system and network security
Basic concepts of cryptographic keys and X.509 certificates
Using GPG and OpenSSL to generate keys and certificates
Concepts of firewalls, VPNs, and IDS
Network storage: NAS, SAN, and RAID
Configuration of a simple computer network
Implementing a network with three perimeters using firewalls
assessment_rules: The final grade is awarded on a scale of thirty. The project presentation and discussion account for 40% of the final grade, while the individual theoretical test accounts for 60%. Honors may be awarded for excellent analytical and design skills, presentation quality, and independence of judgment.
